# Cal/OSHA Heat Illness Prevention Training (General Industry)

> Online course for California general industry employers, supervisors and employees that compares Title 8 CCR Section 3395 (outdoor heat illness prevention) and Section 3396 (indoor heat illness prevention) side by side, with examples from warehouses, plants, kitchens and other non-construction workplaces. Offered by HAZWOPER OSHA Training (https://hazwoper-osha.com).

## Key facts
- Regulations: Title 8 CCR §3395 (outdoor) and §3396 (indoor)
- Duration: 2 hours; 3 lessons plus final exam
- Credits: 0.2 CEU
- Price: $47.99 per seat online or SCORM; virtual instructor-led and in-person group options; volume discounts
- Delivery: 100% online, 24/7; English and Spanish
- Completion window: 3 months; 1 year of access to materials
- Certificate: instant PDF on passing, valid 12 months
- Retraining: the standards set no fixed interval; many employers retrain annually before summer
- Note: employers must also train workers on their own site-specific heat procedures
- Prerequisites: none

## Temperature triggers (from the course FAQ)
- Outdoor: shade required above 80°F; high-heat procedures at 95°F for certain industries such as agriculture and construction
- Indoor: standard applies at 82°F with employees present; additional assessment and controls at 87°F, or at 82°F with restrictive clothing or high radiant heat

## Who it is for
Warehouse, distribution and logistics; manufacturing and foundry; kitchens, bakeries and food processing; laundry and textiles; maintenance and janitorial; retail and grocery; delivery drivers and security officers; supervisors, safety managers, HR and employers.

## Lessons
1. Cal/OSHA Heat Illness Prevention Regulatory Requirements (indoor vs outdoor comparison, written plans)
2. Heat Stress
3. Heat Illness Prevention, Emergency Response, and Case Study (distribution center heat stroke)
